nfb7a522f704.s: Warangal fell to the Tughlaq forces after a five-month siege in:
nfb7a522f704.x: Juna Khan first attacked Warangal in 1321-22; it fell after a five-month siege in 1323, before Ghiyasuddin's death in 1325.

na26ce592278.s: Which Sayyid ruler succeeded Khizr Khan?
na26ce592278.x: The Sayyid order was Khizr Khan, Mubarak Shah, Muhammad Shah and Alauddin Alam Shah.

nindian-history-4-10.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the order of the Delhi Sultanate dynasties?
o: The Khalji dynasty followed the Slave/Mamluk dynasty
The Lodi dynasty followed the Sayyid dynasty
The Sayyid dynasty came before the Khalji dynasty
The Slave/Mamluk dynasty was the first
nindian-history-4-10.x: The order was Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughluq (1320), Sayyid (1414) and Lodi (1451), so the Sayyids came after the Khaljis.

new.s: Who took Delhi in 1414, ending the Tughlaq period?
new.x: Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414, closing the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

new.s: Which of the following was one of the weak successors of Firoz Shah Tughlaq after 1388?
new.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq II and Abu Bakr were weak successors after 1388; Juna Khan was Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the end of the Tughlaq dynasty?
o: Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah was the last Tughlaq Sultan
Timur invaded during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
new.x: Timur invaded in 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah, the last Tughlaq, not under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

new.s: Under Alauddin Khalji, Ghazi Malik served against the Mongols as Governor of:
new.x: Ghazi Malik (later Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq) was Governor of Punjab under Alauddin, guarding against the Mongols.

new.s: Which city of Delhi was built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
new.x: Ghiyasuddin built Tughlaqabad; Siri was Alauddin's and Firozabad and Hisar were Firoz's.

new.s: After the fall of Warangal, the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II died in the river:
new.x: Prataparudra II was taken towards Delhi and died in the Narmada.

new.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Khurasan expedition ended with:
o: The army being destroyed in the hills
new.x: The army raised for Khurasan was disbanded unpaid; destruction in the hills was the fate of the Qarachil expedition.

new.s: The silver coin issued by Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called:
new.x: MBT's silver coin was the Adli; his new gold coin was called Dinar by Ibn Battuta.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's experiment and its result is correctly matched?
o: Khurasan expedition – army destroyed in the hills
Transfer of capital – court stayed at Daulatabad
new.x: Token currency led to mass forgery; the Khurasan army was disbanded unpaid, the Qarachil army was destroyed and the court returned to Delhi.

new.s: In the Sultanate postal system described by Ibn Battuta, 'dawa' couriers travelled:
new.x: Dawa were foot couriers; uluq were horse couriers.

new.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq died at Thatta in 1351 while pursuing the rebel:
new.x: MBT died at Thatta on the way to Sindh, chasing the rebel Taghi after a Gujarat revolt.

new.s: The trial land of Muhammad bin Tughlaq's Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi measured:
new.x: The agriculture department's trial land was 30 × 30 karohs.

new.s: Ibn Battuta wrote his Rihla in:
new.x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla (Kitab-ul-Rihla) was written in Arabic.

new.s: Ibn Battuta was born at:
new.x: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta (1304-1377) was born at Tangiers.

new.s: Which of the following works was written by Barani?
new.x: Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari; Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's autobiography.

new.s: Warangal was recaptured from the Tughlaqs in 1336 by:
new.x: Kapaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family, after Prolaya Nayaka, recaptured Warangal in 1336.

new.s: The Bahmani kingdom (1347) was founded by:
new.x: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) founded the Bahmani kingdom in 1347.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the year 1336:
1. The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded.
2. Kapaya Nayaka recaptured Warangal.
3. The Bahmani kingdom was founded.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Vijayanagara's founding and Kapaya Nayaka's recapture of Warangal both date to 1336; the Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347.

new.s: The Madurai Sultanate was established by:
new.x: Jalaluddin Ahsan Shah established the Madurai Sultanate in 1335.

new.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq abolished about how many taxes?
new.x: Firoz abolished about 24 taxes and kept only the four Islamic taxes.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four Islamic taxes retained by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
new.x: Firoz kept kharaj, jizya, khams and zakat; haq-i-sharb was his irrigation cess.

new.s: Which ruler of Sind agreed to pay tribute to Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
new.x: Jam Babaniya of Sind agreed to pay tribute; Haji Iliyas of Bengal resisted Firoz's two expeditions.

new.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's Diwan-i-Bandagan dealt with:
new.x: Diwan-i-Bandagan looked after about 1,80,000 slaves; charity was Diwan-i-Khairat.

new.s: Under Firoz Shah Tughlaq, Diwan-i-Istihqaq was the department of:
new.x: Diwan-i-Istihqaq handled pensions and grants.

new.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's longest canal, about 150 miles, ran from:
new.x: The Yamuna-Hisar canal (150 miles) was the longest; the Sutlej-Ghaggar canal was 96 miles.

new.s: Firoz Shah's Rajabwah canal was restored in Akbar's time as the:
new.x: The Rajabwah was restored under Akbar as the Shihab (Shahab) Canal.

new.s: Azizuddin Khalid Khani's Persian translation of Sanskrit manuscripts from Jawalamukhi was titled:
new.x: Manuscripts from the Nagarkot campaign were translated as Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi.

new.s: Dagh, the branding of horses, was introduced by:
new.x: Dagh was Alauddin Khalji's measure, not Balban's.

new.s: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa in 1305 for:
new.x: Ain-ul-Mulk Multani won Malwa for Alauddin in 1305 and later served MBT and Firoz.

new.s: The title Zil-i-Ilahi is associated with:
new.x: Zil-i-Ilahi was Balban's title, along with sijda and paibos.

new.s: When Timur sacked Delhi in December 1398, the Sultan was:
new.x: Timur sacked Delhi under Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah, the last Tughlaq.

new.s: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in:
new.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 and shifted the capital there.

new.s: The Sayyid dynasty claimed descent from:
new.x: The Sayyids claimed descent from the Prophet; the other dynasties before them were Turks.

new.s: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate ruled the longest, about 94 years?
new.x: The Tughlaqs ruled 1320-1414, about 94 years.

new.s: Who founded the Lodi dynasty?
new.x: Bahlol Lodi, Governor of Punjab, received the throne from Alam Shah in 1451.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Timur's invasion?
o: It led to the founding of the Mughal Empire
Timur entered Punjab via Multan and Bhatnair
The Tughlaq state broke into regional kingdoms
new.x: The Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in 1526, not as an effect of Timur's invasion.

new.s: Khizr Khan ruled Delhi:
o: As Sultan with the title Ghazi
As a vassal of Bahlol Lodi
As Timur's deputy, without the title of Sultan
new.x: Khizr Khan, Timur's viceroy, ruled as his deputy without taking the title of Sultan.

new.s: The Sayyid ruler Mubarak Shah failed in his campaigns against the:
new.x: Mubarak Shah failed against the Khokhars.

new.s: Which Lodi ruler had the longest reign?
new.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled 1451-89, the longest of the Lodis.

new.s: Sikandar Lodi's original name was:
new.x: Sikandar Lodi was Nizam Khan, third son of Bahlol, crowned on 17 July 1489.

new.s: Nobles opposed to Ibrahim Lodi plotted to enthrone his brother:
new.x: The nobles backed his brother Jalal Khan; Alam Khan was Ibrahim's uncle.

new.s: Ibrahim Lodi seized which fort because it had sheltered Jalal Khan?
new.x: Ibrahim seized Gwalior and made its ruler Vikramajit a vassal.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Lodi dynasty:
1. It was the first Afghan dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.
2. Sikandar Lodi was the son of Bahlol Lodi.
3. Ibrahim Lodi was the brother of Sikandar Lodi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Lodis were the first Afghan dynasty and each ruler was the son of the previous one, so Ibrahim was Sikandar's son, not brother.

new.s: Sikandar Lodi had a Sanskrit work on which subject translated into Persian?
new.x: Despite his harsh religious policy, Sikandar Lodi had a Sanskrit medical work translated into Persian.

new.s: Daulat Khan Lodi, who invited Babur to India, was the Governor of:
new.x: Daulat Khan Lodi was Governor of Punjab.

new.s: At the First Battle of Panipat, Babur's 'Araba' was:
o: A flanking attack on the enemy
A cavalry charge from the rear
Carts chained together as a defence line
new.x: Araba was a line of chained carts, a 'Rumi' (Ottoman) device; Tulughma was the flanking attack.

new.s: Which of the following was one of Babur's gunners at the First Battle of Panipat?
new.x: Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa were Babur's gunners.

new.s: Babur first mentions the use of guns at:
new.x: Babur first mentions guns at Bajaur in 1519; Panipat was the first use of artillery in an Indian battle.

new.s: 21 April 2026 marked which anniversary of the First Battle of Panipat?
new.x: The battle was fought on 21 April 1526, so 2026 marked its 500th anniversary.

new.s: Babur's army at the First Battle of Panipat numbered about:
new.x: Babur had about 12,000 men against Ibrahim's about 1,00,000.

new.s: Babur took the title 'Ghazi' after the Battle of:
new.x: Babur declared Jehad and took the title Ghazi at Khanwa (1527), not Panipat.

new.s: In the Battle of Ghaghra (1529), Babur defeated the:
new.x: At Ghaghra in 1529 Babur defeated the Afghans.

new.s: Jalaluddin Khalji was crowned at:
new.x: Jalaluddin Khalji, founder of the Khalji dynasty, was crowned at Kilokhari.

new.s: The phase of the Slave dynasty under Iltutmish is called the:
new.x: The Slave phases were Qutbi (1206-11), First Ilbari under Iltutmish and Second Ilbari under Balban.

new.s: The Tughlaq dynasty, the longest of the Delhi Sultanate, ruled for about:
new.x: The Tughlaqs ruled 1320-1414, about 94 years; the Khaljis ruled about 30.

new.s: Bahlol Lodi, who had the longest reign among the Delhi Sultans, ruled for about:
new.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled 1451-89, about 38 years.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: The longest reign was Bahlol Lodi's (38 years), not Firoz Shah Tughlaq's (1351-88).

new.s: The fourth floor of the Qutub Minar was damaged during the reign of:
new.x: The Qutub Minar was begun by Aibak, completed by Iltutmish and its fourth floor was damaged in Firoz Shah's time.

new.s: The capital of Qutbuddin Aibak was:
new.x: Aibak ruled from Lahore; Iltutmish was the first Sultan to shift his capital to Delhi.

new.s: Who directly succeeded Iltutmish on the throne of Delhi?
new.x: The Slave line ran Iltutmish → Ruknuddin Firoz → Razia → Bahram Shah.

new.s: In the Slave dynasty, Balban came to the throne after:
new.x: Balban was wazir and heir of Nasiruddin Mahmud; Kaiqubad followed Balban.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sayyid dynasty:
1. Mubarak Shah succeeded Khizr Khan.
2. Muhammad Shah was the last Sayyid ruler.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Mubarak Shah followed Khizr Khan, but the last Sayyid was Alam Shah, who followed Muhammad Shah.

new.s: The Nasiruddin Mahmud who ruled just before Balban belonged to the:
new.x: There were two Nasiruddin Mahmuds: one in the Slave line before Balban and one the last Tughlaq.

new.s: Siri was founded by:
new.x: Siri was Alauddin Khalji's city; Tughlaqabad was Ghiyasuddin's.

new.s: Jaunpur, Hisar and Firozabad were founded by:
new.x: Jaunpur, Hisar, Firozabad and Fatehabad were Firoz Shah Tughlaq's towns.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi (1504); token currency was MBT's, Tughlaqabad Ghiyasuddin's and Siri Alauddin's.

new.s: The title 'Sikandar-i-Sani' (Second Alexander) was assumed by:
new.x: Alauddin Khalji called himself Sikandar-i-Sani; Gulrukhi was Sikandar Lodi's pen name.

new.s: Balban's title Zil-i-Ilahi means:
new.x: Zil-i-Ilahi (Zillillah) means Shadow of God; Lakh Baksh means giver of lakhs.

new.s: Qutbuddin Aibak did not take the title Sultan and ruled as:
new.x: Aibak ruled as Malik; Sultan-i-Azam was Iltutmish's title.

new.s: The last Khalji ruler, Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, was killed by:
new.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah (1316-20) was killed by Khusrau Khan.

new.s: The last effective ruler of the Slave dynasty, killed in 1290, was:
new.x: Kaiqubad was killed in 1290; his infant son Kayumars was only the nominal last ruler.

new.s: When Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, Vijayanagara was ruled by:
new.x: In 1498 Sikandar Lodi ruled Delhi, the Zamorin Calicut and Immadi Narasimha Vijayanagara.

new.s: At Chandawar (1194), Muhammad Ghori defeated:
new.x: Ghori beat Jaichand at Chandawar (1194); Prithviraj was beaten at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).

new.s: Iltutmish crushed Nasiruddin Qabacha, ruler of Multan and Sindh, in:
new.x: Qabacha was crushed in 1228; Yalduz was beaten at Tarain in 1215-16.

new.s: Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in 1221 while chasing:
new.x: Chengiz Khan pursued the Khwarezm prince Jalaluddin Mangbarni, whom Iltutmish refused shelter.

new.s: Chengiz Khan's Mongols reached the Indus in the year:
new.x: Chengiz Khan reached the Indus in 1221 during Iltutmish's reign.

new.s: The Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur was annexed in 1476 by:
new.x: Jaunpur, founded by Khwaja Jahan under the last Tughlaq, was annexed by Bahlol Lodi in 1476.

new.s: Who made Bengal independent of Delhi and withstood Firoz Shah Tughlaq's two campaigns?
new.x: Haji Iliyas made Bengal independent; Tughril Khan's earlier revolt was crushed by Balban.
